page: Microsoft Azure NC40ads_H100_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine from the NCadsH100v5 family, designed for high-performance computing and machine learning workloads. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V84 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, delivering 40 physical cores and 40 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core allocation. The hardware configuration includes 320.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU equipped with 94 GB of VRAM. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 3971 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong performance across multiple vectors. The server achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 23376.0, placing it in the top 10% tier, and a Passmark memory score of 3177.48, also in the top 10%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 525.91 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations perform at 100.89 million operations per second. Large-block memory read bandwidth is measured at 182.31 GB/sec, which sits in the middle 50% tier, representing a potential bottleneck compared to the top-tier cached read bandwidth of 5952.26 GB/sec. For language model execution, the server generates 286.08 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 33.22 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the NC40ads_H100_v5 offers high resource density by combining a top-tier accelerator with a high-frequency AMD EPYC processor and substantial local NVMe storage. This dense integration reduces the need for multi-node clustering for moderately sized models, optimizing resource utilization. The server is suited for workloads such as large language model inference, deep learning training, high-performance database operations, and compute-intensive scientific simulations.
